peers.name: emil-design-eng
peers.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great. Use when building or reviewing a UI component's interactions and polish (press and hover states, popover origin, tooltip timing, transitions vs keyframes, clip-path techniques, drag details) and no narrower skill fits.

peers.name: review-animations
peers.description: Reviews animation and motion code against a high craft bar derived from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy. Default to flagging; approval is earned.

peers.name: apple-design
peers.description: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.

peers.name: animation-vocabulary
peers.description: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.

en.tagline: Turns design corrections into written rules for agents
en.summary: learn-taste reads a session's design corrections and turns each one into a rule with its reason. Rules go into DESIGN.md, a project skill, or a lint check, where the next agent reads them. It writes rules only and never changes component code.
problem: A user corrects an agent's UI work, but the correction only lasts for that session. If it is not written down, the next session makes the same mistake and the user corrects it again.
This skill finds the corrections, including silent edits and repeated nudges, and proposes each one as a rule with a why. Nothing is written until the user approves it.
fit: A project where the user keeps correcting shadows, spacing, or motion values
A team that wants UI taste recorded in DESIGN.md for future agent sessions
Rules that a lint check or token restriction can enforce
unfit: One-off choices for a single page or campaign
Functional bugs or content changes that are not about taste
steps: It reads the current session from the first turn, plus any past session transcripts the user names.
It lists each taste correction from explicit remarks, silent edits, repeated nudges, reverts, and confirmed choices.
It filters out one-off choices and checks whether an existing rule already covers each correction.
It generalizes each correction to a class of components and attaches a why from the user, or marks a proposed why as inferred.
Where code matching can catch a violation, it proposes a lint rule, token restriction, or test; other rules go into DESIGN.md.
It writes only the items the user approves, and asks the user to answer its open questions first.

zh.tagline: 把设计修正记成规则，供后续 agent 读取
zh.summary: learn-taste 读取会话中的设计修正，把每一条转成带原因的规则。规则会写入 DESIGN.md、项目 skill 或 lint 检查，供下一个 agent 读取。它只写规则，不修改组件代码。
problem: 用户纠正 agent 的界面做法，但这些纠正通常只在当次会话内有效。如果没有写下来，下次会话还会犯同样的错，用户还得再纠正一次。
这个 skill 会找出这些纠正，包括静默修改和反复微调，并把每条提议为带原因的规则。用户确认之前，不会写入任何内容。
fit: 用户多次纠正阴影、间距或动效数值的项目
希望把界面品味记录在 DESIGN.md 中，供后续会话使用的团队
规则可以用 lint 检查或 token 限制来强制执行的场景
unfit: 只适用于某一个页面或活动的一次性选择
功能性 bug 或与品味无关的内容修改
steps: 从第一轮开始读取当前会话，并读取用户指定的历史会话记录。
列出每一条品味修正，包括明确的意见、静默修改、反复微调、撤销和已确认的选择。
过滤掉一次性选择，并检查现有规则是否已经覆盖每一条修正。
把每条修正推广到一类组件，附上用户的原因；若原因是推断的，则标注为 inferred。
如果能通过代码匹配发现违规，就提议 lint 规则、token 限制或测试；其余规则写入 DESIGN.md。
只写入用户批准的条目，并先请用户回答其中的待确认问题。
